slides.say: A spelling test has between ten and twenty-five words, inclusive. Each of fourteen students spells at least one fifth of the words correctly. What are the smallest and the largest possible totals of correctly spelled words in the class?

So they ask for a minimum and a maximum, the smallest and the biggest total for the whole class. [short pause] We'll solve it in two different ways, by understanding which way to push, and then with the last digit.

[short pause] Let's start by understanding. To push the total to an extreme, we push everything around it. Let's start with one student. For the fewest correct words, the test is the shortest, ten words, and he spells the smallest share, one fifth. One fifth of ten is ten divided by five, which is two words.

Fourteen students with two each is fourteen times two, twenty-eight. Choice numbers one and four start with seventy, not twenty-eight, so they're out. Seventy is one fifth of the longest test, five words each. But for the fewest, the test is the shortest too.

Now let's find the most. The longest test has twenty-five words. Careful here, at least one fifth doesn't mean exactly one fifth. A student can spell all the words right. So one student spells at most twenty-five.
For the whole class it's fourteen times twenty-five. Ten times twenty-five is two hundred fifty. Four times twenty-five is a hundred. Two hundred fifty plus a hundred is three hundred fifty.
at: Two hundred fifty plus a hundred

slides.say: A hundred forty in choice number two is fourteen times ten, the shortest test, all correct. That's not the most. So the class spells between twenty-eight and three hundred fifty words, and choice number three is our answer.
at: choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now with the last digit. Remember, the last digit of a product comes only from the last digits. The fewest is the shortest test, ten words, and one fifth of it, two words, for each of fourteen students.

So it's fourteen times two. Look only at the last digits. Four times two is eight, so the total ends in eight. Twenty-eight ends in eight, and seventy ends in zero. So choice numbers one and four are out.
at: so choice numbers one and four

slides.say: The most is the longest test, all twenty-five words, for each of fourteen students. Here the last digit can't help. Three hundred fifty and a hundred forty both end in zero.

So here we simply multiply. Fourteen times twenty-five is three hundred fifty. The last digit helps only when the choices end in different digits. Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
